newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil says Aasgard oil ship delayed.
newsitem.headline: Statoil says Aasgard oil ship delayed.

text.p: The Aasgard A production ship will be delivered to Aker Stord in western Norway a few weeks behind schedule, but start up of the Aasgard development off mid-Norway should not be affected, operator Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday.
Statoil said the delay was due to capacity problems at Japan's Hitachi Zosen yard, where the hull is under construction.

Aasgard A is now expected to reach Aker in January, 1998 rather than in December, 1997. Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said the slippage would be made up either at the yard or in the offshore commissioning phase.

The vessel, ranked as the world's largest oil production monohull, is due to come on stream in October, 1998. It will have capacity to process some 200,000 barrels per day (bpd) and to store more than 900,000 bpd.
